article_title: The Impact of Virtual Trips on the Development of Arabic Language Oral Skills among Third Grade Students in Jordan
citation: Nail M. Alhajya, Sumaia S. Alzaghamim, Yousef M. Arouri. (2018). THE IMPACT OF VIRTUAL TRIPS ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF ARABIC LANGUAGE ORAL SKILLS AMONG THIRD GRADE STUDENTS IN JORDAN. Journal of Technology and Science Education, 8(1), 72-85. https://doi.org/10.3926/jotse.331
title: Virtual Trips Model (VTM) for third-grade Arabic oral skills
description: The Virtual Trips Model is an interactive teaching method the researchers designed for third-grade Arabic oral skills, defined as "a process of simulating a realistic or fictional environment that is photographed and built through technology supported by images, 3D images, and graphics". It comprised three 3D videos of Jordanian touristic sites (Petra, Aqaba, Al-Karak Castle) with sound and image, daily lesson plans, a 3D camera, and a 3D screen with glasses, applied over one month and validated by arbitrators.
requirements: Hardware and software creating the virtual environment, including a 3D camera and a 3D screen with 3D screen glasses
Teacher training on applying VTM in the classroom environment
Content validated by a panel of arbitrators for presentation, time, and quality of images and sound
constraints: Studied only with third-grade students in one public school in Tafila Governorate, Jordan, on three units of the Arabic third-grade textbook in the 2015-2016 second term
target_learning_goals: Arabic language oral skills (listening comprehension and interaction)
examples: The experimental group was taught with VTM for one month while the control group received traditional teaching for the same amount of time, with the same teacher participating in lesson-plan preparation
key_sources: Nail M. Alhajya, Sumaia S. Alzaghamim, Yousef M. Arouri. (2018). THE IMPACT OF VIRTUAL TRIPS ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF ARABIC LANGUAGE ORAL SKILLS AMONG THIRD GRADE STUDENTS IN JORDAN. Journal of Technology and Science Education, 8(1), 72-85. https://doi.org/10.3926/jotse.331

article_title: Development of an electrosurgery-compatible simulation task for quantitatively assessing oral cancer resection skills: initial validity evidence.
citation: Sakamoto Kayo, Mitani Sohei, Nishio Naoki, Kitani Takashi, Sato Eriko, Tanaka Keiko, Ugumori Toru, Wakisaka Hiroyuki, Hato Naohito. (2026). Development of an electrosurgery-compatible simulation task for quantitatively assessing oral cancer resection skills: initial validity evidence. BMC Medical Education, 26, 408. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-08743-5
title: Electrosurgery-compatible plant-derived (VTT) oral cancer resection simulation task with a 15 mm phantom tumor and 10 mm safety margin design
description: A soft-tissue simulation task built by modifying a commercially available Versatile Training Tissue (VTT) model made of konjac potato flour, whose glucomannan content turns black with carbonization above 200 °C, enabling replication of electrosurgery. The task uses a 15 mm hemispherical phantom tumor buried in tissue and requires a 10 mm safety margin in all directions. Surgeons work alone with a monopolar handpiece in the dominant hand and DeBakey forceps in the non-dominant hand.
requirements: An electrosurgical unit (VIO50C) with a coagulation-mode monopolar handpiece and DeBakey forceps, plus a spectral colorimeter and ruler for assessment
constraints: The phantom tumor is hemispherical with a distinct color, whereas actual oral tumors are often irregular, not clearly visible, and extend deeper than they appear, requiring palpation
target_learning_goals: Minimizing thermal tissue damage during electrosurgery
examples: The authors tried prototypes with 10 mm, 15 mm, and 20 mm phantom tumors and selected the 15 mm hemispherical tumor for usability
key_sources: Sakamoto Kayo, Mitani Sohei, Nishio Naoki, Kitani Takashi, Sato Eriko, Tanaka Keiko, Ugumori Toru, Wakisaka Hiroyuki, Hato Naohito. (2026). Development of an electrosurgery-compatible simulation task for quantitatively assessing oral cancer resection skills: initial validity evidence. BMC Medical Education, 26, 408. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-08743-5

article_title: Virtual Reality in Training and Assessment Among Clinical Students and Lecturers at a Nigerian University: A Phenomenological Study.
citation: Komolafe AO et al. (2026). Virtual Reality in Training and Assessment Among Clinical Students and Lecturers at a Nigerian University: A Phenomenological Study. JMIR Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.2196/75021
title: VTRACS: a haptic-limited VR simulation platform for training and assessing clinical students
description: VTRACS (Virtual reality model to TRain and Assess Clinical Students) is a VR platform that delivered "immersive clinical scenarios through standalone VR headsets (Meta Quest 2)" across Nursing, Dentistry, Medicine, and Surgery. Simulations replicated scenarios such as "performing vital signs checks, abdominal examinations... and conducting tooth extraction." Participants interacted via hand-held controllers; haptic feedback "was limited to vibrations; no tactile sensations or physical resistance were simulated." Sessions lasted 20-25 minutes in a controlled laboratory with technical support.
requirements: Standalone VR headsets (Meta Quest 2), hand-held controllers, and a controlled laboratory environment with technical support available throughout sessions
constraints: Haptic feedback was limited to vibrations; no tactile sensations or physical resistance were simulated
target_learning_goals: clinical skill acquisition and clinical examination competence
examples: 24 clinical students were trained and assessed on clinical scenarios in their field of study, with two supervised exposures before interviews
key_sources: Komolafe AO et al. (2026). Virtual Reality in Training and Assessment Among Clinical Students and Lecturers at a Nigerian University: A Phenomenological Study. JMIR Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.2196/75021

article_title: Virtual Reality in Training and Assessment Among Clinical Students and Lecturers at a Nigerian University: A Phenomenological Study.
citation: Komolafe AO et al. (2026). Virtual Reality in Training and Assessment Among Clinical Students and Lecturers at a Nigerian University: A Phenomenological Study. JMIR Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.2196/75021
title: Five-theme experiential framework of VR use in clinical training: excitement, usability, proficiency, challenges, and uniformity
description: The study organizes participants' experiences with VTRACS into "5 major themes and 13 nodes": expression of excitement (novice, complementary learning method, imagination rather than reality), simple and useful innovation (ease of use, compatible with the task), proficiency enhancement (unlimited learning access, confidence, fewer medical errors), challenges with innovation (limited patient complexity and feedback, loss of empathy, financial burden), and uniformity (standardized scenarios, objectivity). Lecturers reported more concerns than students, attributed to generational differences.
requirements: Direct participant experience with VR training and assessment, gathered through focus group discussions and in-depth interviews
constraints: Findings are based on a relatively smaller, nonrepresentative sample and are context-dependent rather than universally applicable
target_learning_goals: understanding learner and educator experiences of VR-based clinical training and assessment
examples: 13 nodes such as ease of use, confidence, fewer medical errors, and standardized clinical scenarios were derived from NVivo thematic analysis of 4 FGDs and 8 IDIs
key_sources: Komolafe AO et al. (2026). Virtual Reality in Training and Assessment Among Clinical Students and Lecturers at a Nigerian University: A Phenomenological Study. JMIR Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.2196/75021
